feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning in digital communications and strategy. It shows solid progression, relevant technical depth, and good mission-driven alignment, but it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer repeated ideas, and more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level leadership and then consulting work; this supports credibility and growth.  
- Strong blend of strategy, operations, technical execution, and communications leadership, with useful tools/platforms named throughout.  
- Good use of scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers,” which adds impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: include results like engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign impact, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication across Summary, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; the CV currently repeats similar themes and tools, which weakens sharpness.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around leadership, public-sector relevance, and measurable platform/program ownership would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more specific positioning tied to enterprise web, content operations, and advocacy/public-sector communications.
- Emphasize recent leadership scope: digital strategy, platform modernization, analytics, and cross-functional governance for mission-driven organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, editorial operations, and digital governance. Known for building scalable workflows and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are already reinforced throughout Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, operational, and production capabilities, but several items are broad and overlap heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and making terms more precise will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web operations & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and cleaner grammar.
- Replace one generic item with a more distinctive strength, such as “Workflow automation” or “Platform governance,” to better reflect recent experience.
- Keep phrasing parallel: use noun-based constructions throughout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header summary.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills categories; if both sections remain, this block should stay shorter and more high-level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance improvements to streamline organization-wide communications.”
- Consolidate web build details into one bullet: “Built campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member resource/toolkit experiences in Drupal.”
- Add measurable scope if possible: number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, campaign launches, search accuracy gains, time saved, or publishing efficiency improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Microsite and AI search language overlaps with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale indicators, but it reads a bit like a responsibility list. Tighten around 4–5 outcome-led bullets and emphasize leadership, platform transformation, and measurable operational improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, reporting efficiency, publishing turnaround, or cost savings from the in-house studio.
- Combine overlapping operational points: merge analytics/governance/planning into one bullet showing business impact, e.g., “Built GA4/Clarity/Power BI/BigQuery reporting and publishing governance frameworks to improve decision-making and cross-department execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; in this entry, stress enterprise ownership and scale rather than day-to-day channel management.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame this here as capacity-building and infrastructure leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before you moved into director-level strategy.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, scaling NACo’s editorial and advocacy communications operations.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Helped improve…” is weak and repeats later governance/workflow themes from the Director role; use stronger ownership language.
- Video studio/multimedia expansion is already covered in the 2022–2024 role, so keep this item focused on launching the recurring video program, not broader video capacity.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance over generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Stakeholder-centered content strategy” or “Content strategy and editorial planning” to sound more senior.
- Keep this section capability-focused; leave execution details and scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to recent experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep it if needed, but avoid repeating “audience-focused” language used elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill set, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-feeling items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is still central to current work.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Enterprise CMS platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to tighten phrasing.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact: “AI-enabled search” and “CMS modernization” deserve prominence because they are reinforced by current and recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and doesn’t yet signal strategic value. In Topline Skills, emphasize decision-making, optimization, and executive reporting over repeating software names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI and measurement framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • Dashboard development (GA4, Power BI, Looker Studio) • User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) • Data analysis with BigQuery • SEO and performance optimization”
- Group tools in parentheses instead of listing each as a separate bullet to improve scanability.
- Replace “KPI design” with “KPI and measurement framework design” for stronger seniority.
- If accurate, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere on the CV, such as “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page website” or “reporting supporting organization-wide decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior and systems-focused, reflecting recent leadership rather than hands-on-only tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Systems & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level terms: **Broadcast-style video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production**
- If space allows, emphasize scope over tools: **End-to-end video and event production** is stronger than separate “video production and editing.”
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if used elsewhere in skills style, e.g. **broadcast-quality studio production** to echo the recent in-house studio build.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially repeat “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in the 2022–2024 Director role; avoid overloading this skills block with lower-level task wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platform: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: **Drupal (enterprise web modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming for clarity and seniority: **CMS & Web Platforms**
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/less-used tools with level cues: **Drupal (advanced) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list broader and the other more outcome- or proficiency-focused.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you add platform-specific context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize current, higher-value tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied capabilities, not languages alone: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add a scope/result cue tied to recent work, e.g., “API integrations for campaign/content workflows” or “GitHub Actions for deployment automation.”
- Order by strategic value and recency: JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS • jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GTM may also fit under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**.
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Teams.
- If accurate, replace weaker/general tools with stronger implementation language: **Airtable workflow systems, Power Automate flows, Zapier integrations**.
- Consider trimming to the most relevant/current tools only: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Basecamp and Trello may add little if Jira/Asana already cover project management depth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too thin to add much value on its own. It should better signal enterprise-level email/engagement capability and align with the strong recent experience leading email operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Expand and sharpen the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If accurate, add one qualifier for scale or use case in parentheses, e.g. **Higher Logic (member communications)** or **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (automation and audience journeys)**
- Keep platform names only if you can’t support outcomes elsewhere; otherwise use this line to show functional depth, not just vendor familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” capability is already well covered in recent NACo roles; avoid repeating newsletter scale or channel leadership here.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, video, and team leadership. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational contributions in this earlier period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage buildout and delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and support multi-channel communications across web, email, social and video.”
- Add clearer scope/results where possible: include website size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstractions: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific outputs like “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy videos, and website content.”
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with 2018–2024 roles; keep this lighter here.
- “providing guidance to a digital media associate” may feel minor/redundant given stronger later leadership titles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize cross-functional coordination and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support role, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia materials for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles; one compact sentence or two bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid repeating video/editorial leadership themes already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
